annex_basis: Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part I - basic equation; no numbered example in annex - constructed from formula

computation.method: Newton / bisection iterative solving for X > -1, monotonic decreasing RHS in X
computation.iterations: f(0.10)= 1019.3 >1000, f(0.20)=977.2 <1000, root bracketed; Newton from 0.15 converges to 0.154489363999254 in 5 iterations tolerance 1e-12

result_aprc.rounding_rule: Annex I Part I remark (d): at least one decimal, round up if following decimal >=5

assumptions_applied: Part I remark (a): t1=0 first drawdown start date
Part I remark (b): intervals expressed in years/fractions of year, year=365 days (366 leap), 12 equal months =365/12=30.416666... days, so k/12 years used
Part I remark (d): rounding to at least one decimal
Part II (a): not needed because drawdown timing fixed; if freedom assumed, total deemed drawn immediately and in full - same result
weakest_point: Assumes equal months = 1/12 year exactly (30.41666 days). Using actual calendar days (28-31) would shift APRC by ~0.1pp; also assumes no additional charges, no (g)(ii) single-sum fee

case_name: Charges paid at conclusion - arrangement fee at t=0
annex_basis: Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part I + Part II (g)(ii) single-sum non-interest charge at conclusion; constructed

result_aprc.rounding_rule: Annex I at least one decimal

assumptions_applied: Part I (b) equal months =1/12 year, t1=0
Part II (g)(ii): non-interest charge expressed as single sum paid at date of conclusion of credit agreement - 50 EUR at sl=0
Part II (g)(iv): final payment clears balance
Part I (d) rounding
weakest_point: Ambiguity whether fee deducted from drawdown (Ck net) vs Dl at t=0; directive includes all charges in Dl on RHS, not netting from Ck; implementation diverging on net vs gross produces different APRC; we applied Dl at t=0 as per (g)(ii)

case_name: Irregular intervals - two repayments at 6 and 12 months
annex_basis: Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part I - irregular interval example; Directive (EU) 2023/2225 Annex III same formula
assumptions_applied: Part I (a) amounts not necessarily equal nor at equal intervals - irregular intervals allowed
Part I (b) interval expressed in years/fractions: 6 months =0.5 year = 182.5 days under 365-day year assumption, 12 months=1.0 year
Part I (c) year=365 days, 366 leap
No Part II additional assumption needed because dates known
weakest_point: Day-count: 6 months as 0.5 year exactly vs 182/365 or 181/365 depending on calendar; annex prescribes equal months =30.41666 days, so 6 months =182.5 days =0.5 year exact under that convention - we used exact 0.5; actual calendar would differ

case_name: Two drawdowns irregular - shows tk handling
annex_basis: Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part I - multiple drawdowns example; assumption (a) vs fixed dates
assumptions_applied: Part I (a): t1=0, tk interval between first drawdown and subsequent drawdowns
Part I (b): 3 months =0.25 year under equal-month convention 365/12*3=91.25 days

Part II (a): If freedom of drawdown, total deemed drawn immediately and in full - NOT applied here because drawdown dates contractually fixed, so actual dates used; if (a) were applied, Ck would be 1000 at t=0 leading to higher APRC
Part II (f)(ii): if date of initial drawdown unknown, shortest interval assumption - not needed here
weakest_point: If lender argues freedom of drawdown under (a), would treat second 500 as drawn at t=0, increasing present value of drawdowns and raising APRC; distinction between fixed schedule vs free drawdown is key implementation divergence

annex_basis: Directive 2008/48/EC Annex I Part II (d) overdraft and (h) ceiling EUR 1500 - official assumptions; Directive 2011/90/EU replacement text

drawdowns.assumption: Part II (d) total amount deemed drawn in full and for whole duration; Part II (h) ceiling EUR 1500 if not agreed

repayments.note: repayment after 3 months includes 20 EUR interest/charges
repayments.assumption: Part II (d) if duration unknown, APRC calculated assuming duration 3 months

assumptions_applied: Part II (d): overdraft total amount deemed drawn in full and for whole duration; if duration not known, 3 months assumed - we applied 3 months =0.25 year
Part II (h): if ceiling not agreed, assumed EUR 1500 - we used 1500
Part I (b): 3 months =0.25 year using equal months 30.41666 days *3 =91.25 days =0.25 year under 365-day year; year=365 days (366 leap)
Part I (d) rounding at least one decimal
Part II (g)(i): interest paid with capital - included in 1520
doc_vs_general: probably - overdraft 3-month assumption is verbatim from annex, 1500 ceiling is verbatim, but numeric 1520 repayment is constructed
weakest_point: Real overdraft may have daily interest accrual and fees per day; using 0.25 year exact vs 90 days vs 91.25 days changes APRC; also leap year 366 would change year fraction; flagged as convention-sensitive; assumption (d) says 3 months, but does not specify if 90 days or 91.25 days - we used equal-month 0.25 year as per Part I (b) convention
